domain: Hot electronics (Si, SOI, SiC, GaN, Ga2O3, diamond, vacuum/NEMS; hot memory) and solar power conversion (c-Si, tandems, III-V, hot PV, TPV, heat engines; Mercury manufacturability), 2026-2300
summary: HOT COMPUTE IS NOT AN ARCHITECTURAL LEVER; PV PHYSICS AND SUNLIGHT ARE. (1) Every thermionic switch - Si, SiC, GaN, Ga2O3, diamond - obeys the Boltzmann floor SS = ln10 kT/q (71 mV/dec at 85 C, 114 at 300 C, 153 at 500 C), so switching energy scales as T^2: x1.12 at 105 C, x2.6 at 300 C, x4.7 at 500 C even for perfect devices. On top, 2026 wide-bandgap logic is 1e4-1e7 x worse per op (NASA SiC JFET-R ICs: 6 um, +25/-10 V, 175-195 transistors, >1 yr at 500 C; GaN E/D-mode 5 V; HiTSiC CMOS 15 V at 300 C); the gap may close to ~1000x (2040), ~30x (2070), ~5x (2100+). Hot Si: qualified to 150-175 C, SOI 225 C continuous; Si ni at 300 C is x3400 its 85 C value and Cu electromigration allows 1/16 of the current at 200 C, 1/110 at 300 C. Dense memory stops near 150 C (MRAM/RRAM); only AlScN ferro-diodes (600 C, 60 h) and bit-scale SiC/GaN SRAM survive 300-500 C. (2) PV: a one-diode c-Si model calibrated to 20 % AM0 gives -0.34 %/K for a thin IBC cell (the project's -0.42 %/K matches legacy Voc 0.60 V cells) and eta ~ 0 near 575-600 K. The AM0 Shockley-Queisser limit is 30.2 % at 301 K, 23.6 % at 473 K, 14.5 % at 773 K. The film temperature is set by alpha, eps and coverage, never by eta (chips re-dissipate the electricity in the same sheet). (3) Placement (f=0.01): Tj 85/105/125/200/300/500 C puts sails at 0.92/0.82/0.74/0.52/0.35/0.19 AU; the closed-shell floor moves 1.36/1.22/1.10/0.76/0.52/0.27 AU. With Mercury-buildable c-Si, FLOP/s per kg at 105/125 C is -6/-13 % (2026 logic) or within +/-4 % (2100+ logic) of 85 C and falls beyond ~150 C (-11 to -66 % at 200 C), while FLOP per joule of sunlight always falls (-17 % at 105, -31 % at 125 C, 2100+). Even an ideal hot film (SQ-limit PV, Boltzmann-floor logic) gains only 1.3-1.6x FLOP/s/kg at 200-300 C and loses 2-4x sunlight efficiency; a Mercury-built swarm is close to the sunlight limit, so cold wins. (4) Where is the swarm: the rock-limited swarm (4e22 kg delivered) sits OUTSIDE Earth's orbit at 1.11-1.24 AU (f 0.49-0.73) for Tj 60-85 C; keeping it inside 1 AU needs Tj >= 116-130 C and costs 16-20 % of the swarm's compute (full shell: Tj >= 137-141 C, -50-63 %). (5) Concentration: hot pods shrink radiators (1.45 g/W at 85 C -> 0.20 at 300 C) but wings and module dominate; the film stays 4.8-8.4x better per kg and pods' own optimum Tj is flat 85-150 C. (6) Mercury-buildable PV is silicon only: perovskites are iodine-limited (f <= 1e-5), III-V In/Ge-limited (f <= 3e-6; 3e-3 at 1000x concentration). Heat engines and solar TPV cost 2.3-3.7x the film's mass per W (incl. chip cooling). (7) Combined 2100+ (30 % all-Si tandem, alpha 0.80, 0.135 kg/m2): r 0.85-0.69 AU (Tj 85-125 C), 410-545 W/m2, pitch 19-17 mm, film 0.30-0.38 g/W, swarm 1.8e+18 FLOP/s/kg (x201 vs 2026) and 1.6e+14 FLOP/J of sunlight (x95).

architecture_implications.question: How hot can dense compute run (Part 1)?
architecture_implications.answer: Dense, efficient logic stays at Tj 85-125 C in every era. Si is qualified to 150-175 C and SOI to 225 C (300 C excursions), but intrinsic leakage (ni x180 at 200 C, x3400 at 300 C vs 85 C) and electromigration (1/16 of the current at 200 C) stop leading-edge density there. SiC/GaN/Ga2O3/diamond and vacuum/NEMS devices run at 300-800 C, but today at 1e4-1e7 x the energy per op and 1e-5-1e-7 of the density; even at maturity the Boltzmann floor adds x2.6 at 300 C and x4.7 at 500 C. Dense NVM stops near 150 C; AlScN ferro-diodes (600 C) are the only hot-memory candidate and need Sc.

architecture_implications.question: What would hot compute do to the swarm (Part 2)?
architecture_implications.answer: It lets sails sit closer (Tj 85/105/125/200/300/500 C -> 0.92/0.82/0.74/0.52/0.35/0.19 AU at f=0.01) and moves the full-shell cavity floor from 1.36 to 1.10 (125 C), 0.76 (200 C), 0.52 (300 C) AU. But c-Si loses efficiency, the Mg spreader fails above ~400 K, meteoroid overbuild rises (0.10 -> 0.33 at 0.35 AU) and logic pays T^2. Net FLOP/s/kg at 105/125 C is -6/-13 % (2026 logic) or flat within 4 % (2100+ logic) and drops beyond ~150 C; FLOP per joule of sunlight falls monotonically. Even the ideal hot film (SQ PV + Boltzmann-floor logic) is only 1.3-1.6x better per kg at 200-300 C and 2-4x worse per joule of sunlight.

architecture_implications.question: Does hot logic favour concentration or distribution?
architecture_implications.answer: Distribution, still. A pod decouples its PV wing (kept at ~350 K) from hot chips, and hot radiators shrink as T^4 (1.45 g/W at 85 C -> 0.71 at 150 C -> 0.20 at 300 C), but the wing (0.38-0.66 g/W) and module/loops/shield (1.0-2.1 g/W) do not shrink and the chips pay the same T^2 energy. Best-credible pods stay 4.7x (2026) to 8.4x (2100+) worse per kg than the film; lite 1 kg/kW pods 3.1-5.6x. The pod optimum Tj is flat 85-150 C. Better PV widens the gap, because it lightens the film (whose mass is PV) but not the pod module: each 1 % of power moved to pods costs ~3.4 % of swarm mass in 2026 and ~7 % in 2100+.

architecture_implications.question: Does it change where the swarm is (inside or outside Earth orbit)?
architecture_implications.answer: Only if we pay for it. With Mercury rock (4e22 kg delivered) the best swarm is cold and sits OUTSIDE Earth at 1.11-1.24 AU with f 0.49-0.73; a whole-planet swarm closes the sky (f=1) at 1.33-1.58 AU. Pulling it inside 1 AU needs Tj 116-130 C (rock) or 137-141 C (closed shell) and costs 16-20 % (rock) or 50-63 % (closed shell, vs a 60 C shell) of the swarm compute. Hot logic therefore makes an Earth-interior swarm possible at a known price; it is a policy choice, not a free gain.

architecture_implications.question: PV and power conversion (Part 3)
architecture_implications.answer: Silicon is the only Mercury-scale absorber: thin c-Si 20 % -> 22.5 % (2040) -> 24 % (2070) AM0; 25-30 % needs a Mercury-native wide-gap top cell (Si nanocrystals in SiO2 are the only candidate made of Si and O, and are at Voc <= 0.37-0.5 V today). Perovskites (Pb, I, Br, Cs, organics, ITO In) are capped at f <= 1e-5 by iodine; III-V by In/Ge/As (f <= 3e-6, or 3e-3 at 1000x concentration with actively cooled cells). Hot PV: the AM0 SQ limit is 23.7 % at 200 C and 14.5 % at 500 C; no Mercury-native wide-gap cell exists. Heat engines (best 2-3 g/W with chip cooling) and solar TPV (>= 1.6 g/W_e before chips, 6.8 % demonstrated) lose to the 0.88 g/W film. The cheapest gain is optical: reflect the 25.5 % of AM0 below the Si gap (alpha 0.90 -> 0.80).

architecture_implications.question: Combined (Part 4): PV 25-35 % plus hot-tolerant logic
architecture_implications.answer: Higher PV efficiency does NOT cool the film: the chips re-dissipate the extra electricity in the same sheet, so T and orbit are unchanged at fixed alpha/eps/f (checked: 347.97 K at eta 20, 30, 35 %). It raises chip W/m2 in proportion, so pitch shrinks (0.15 W chiplets: 26.8 -> 19.1 mm) and g/W falls. A pod wing does run cooler with higher eta, because its electricity leaves the wing. Combined 2100+ (30 % all-Si tandem, alpha 0.80, 0.135 kg/m2): f=0.01 orbit 0.85 AU at Tj 85 C or 0.69 AU at 125 C; 410-545 W/m2; film 0.30-0.38 g/W; swarm 1.8-1.9e18 FLOP/s/kg; 1.1-1.6e14 FLOP/J of sunlight. Full shell: 1.33 AU (85 C) or 1.07 AU (125 C). Sail/pod balance stays set by memory and interconnect roles (pods 0.3-1 %).

architecture_implications.question: Interactions with studies 1-3
architecture_implications.answer: Higher W/m2 shrinks the film area available per W (4785 -> 1840-2440 mm2/W), which collides with adiabatic logic's 611-2050 mm2/W (study 1) in 2100+, especially if hotter/closer. Memory (study 2) also caps Tj near 150 C. Interconnect (study 3) is unaffected by temperature, but denser chiplets help mesh hop energy. Closer orbits raise chip dose ~r^-2 (x1.8 at 0.69 AU, x7 at 0.35 AU) on top of 150-470 krad per 10 yr at 0.92 AU.

wildcards.wildcard: Mercury-native wide-gap top cell works (Si nanocrystals in SiO2, or a Ca/Mg/Ti/S compound) -> all-Si tandem at 30-35 % AM0
wildcards.effect: FLOP/s per kg x1.25-1.45 and per joule of sunlight x1.25-1.45 vs c-Si at 24 %; orbit unchanged.

wildcards.wildcard: Steep-slope, temperature-insensitive switch (field-emission vacuum nano-transistor, NEMS, TFET) at <= 3x Si energy
wildcards.effect: Breaks the T^2 law: hot pods with cold PV wings and 300-500 C radiators become ~1.5-2x lighter (radiators 0.06-0.2 g/W), narrowing film/pod to ~2-3x; the film is still PV-limited.

wildcards.wildcard: Hot-carrier, thermoradiative or intermediate-band cells beyond the SQ limit
wildcards.effect: A cell that gains from heat would flip the Part-2 trade; none has shown net gain.

wildcards.wildcard: Self-annealing hot PV (displacement damage anneals at 150-300 C)
wildcards.effect: Lets wide-gap cells sit at 0.3-0.5 AU without radiation loss; only useful if logic also runs hot.

wildcards.wildcard: Ga/Ge from Mercury's core (siderophile enrichment) enables III-V concentrator pods at f ~ 1e-3-1e-2
wildcards.effect: A 30-35 % pod wing class; does not change the film.

wildcards.wildcard: Earth-interior swarm mandated (sunlight corridor to Earth)
wildcards.effect: Forces Tj 116-141 C and costs 16-63 % of compute; hot logic becomes worth developing for this reason alone.
